body: A urinary tract infection happens when germs infect part of the urinary system. It may affect the bladder, kidney, prostate, or urine passage.
Many UTIs improve with the right antibiotic. Recurrent UTI, fever, kidney pain, and infection in men need careful evaluation.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Common symptoms include burning urine, frequent urination, urgency, lower abdominal pain, cloudy urine, bad smell, blood in urine, fever, chills, side pain, or weakness.
A kidney infection may cause fever, chills, vomiting, and side or back pain.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if UTI keeps coming back, fever is present, pain is severe, urine has blood, or symptoms do not improve.
Men with UTI symptoms should be evaluated because infection may be linked to prostate, stones, blockage, or incomplete emptying.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Tests may include urine routine, urine culture, blood tests, ultrasound, post-void residual urine check, CT scan, cystoscopy, or prostate evaluation when needed.
The aim is to confirm infection, choose the right antibiotic, and find why infections keep returning.

experience.title: Treatment options for UTI
body: Simple UTI may need a short medicine course. Recurrent UTI needs a deeper look.
Options may include culture-based antibiotics, pain relief, hydration advice, prevention steps, and treatment of stones, prostate blockage, stricture, or incomplete emptying.

careGuide.title: Before, during, and after UTI care
careGuide.intro: UTI care should treat the infection and look for causes when infection repeats.

tabs.label: Before Treatment
items: Share fever, chills, or side pain

tabs.label: After Treatment
items: Return if fever or pain appears

careGuide.note: Your plan will depend on symptoms, culture report, recurrence pattern, and scan findings.

items.question: Can I take antibiotics without a urine culture?
items.answer: Sometimes urgent treatment is needed, but recurrent or unclear UTI should be guided by urine culture.

items.question: Why does UTI keep coming back?
items.answer: Possible causes include poor emptying, stones, blockage, prostate issues, diabetes, or resistant bacteria.

items.question: Is fever with UTI serious?
items.answer: Fever, chills, vomiting, or side pain may suggest kidney infection and needs prompt care.

items.question: Do men need evaluation for UTI?
items.answer: Yes. UTI in men should be reviewed for prostate, stone, stricture, or emptying problems.

items.question: Can UTI be prevented?
items.answer: Prevention depends on the cause. Hydration, bladder habits, culture review, and treating underlying problems may help.
